server_settings.name: autovacuum_vacuum_threshold

server_settings.name: client_encoding

server_settings.name: DateStyle

server_settings.extra_desc: This affects real, double precision, and geometric data types. A zero or negative parameter value is added to the standard number of digits (FLT_DIG or DBL_DIG as appropriate). Any value greater than zero selects precise output mode.

server_settings.name: icu_validation_level

server_settings.name: timezone_abbreviations

server_settings.name: client_min_messages
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the message levels that are sent to the client.
server_settings.extra_desc: Each level includes all the levels that follow it. The later the level, the fewer messages are sent.

server_settings.name: createrole_self_grant
server_settings.short_desc: Sets whether a CREATEROLE user automatically grants the role to themselves, and with which options.

server_settings.name: default_table_access_method

server_settings.name: default_tablespace

server_settings.name: default_toast_compression

server_settings.name: default_transaction_deferrable

server_settings.name: default_transaction_isolation
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the transaction isolation level of each new transaction.

server_settings.name: default_transaction_read_only
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the default read-only status of new transactions.

server_settings.name: event_triggers
server_settings.short_desc: Enables event triggers.
server_settings.extra_desc: When enabled, event triggers will fire for all applicable statements.

server_settings.name: gin_pending_list_limit
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum size of the pending list for GIN index.

server_settings.name: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum allowed idle time between queries, when in a transaction.
server_settings.extra_desc: A value of 0 turns off the timeout.

server_settings.name: idle_session_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum allowed idle time between queries, when not in a transaction.
server_settings.extra_desc: A value of 0 turns off the timeout.

server_settings.name: lock_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum allowed duration of any wait for a lock.
server_settings.extra_desc: A value of 0 turns off the timeout.

server_settings.name: restrict_nonsystem_relation_kind

server_settings.name: row_security

server_settings.name: search_path

server_settings.name: session_replication_role
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the session's behavior for triggers and rewrite rules.

server_settings.name: statement_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum allowed duration of any statement.
server_settings.extra_desc: A value of 0 turns off the timeout.

server_settings.name: temp_tablespaces
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the tablespace(s) to use for temporary tables and sort files.

server_settings.name: transaction_deferrable

server_settings.name: transaction_isolation

server_settings.name: transaction_read_only
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the current transaction's read-only status.

server_settings.name: transaction_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum allowed duration of any transaction within a session (not a prepared transaction).
server_settings.extra_desc: A value of 0 turns off the timeout.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies which classes of statements will be logged by session audit logging. Multiple classes can be provided using a comma-separated list and classes can be subtracted by prefacing the class with a - sign.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_catalog
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies that session logging should be enabled in the case where all relations in a statement are in pg_catalog.  Disabling this setting will reduce noise in the log from tools like psql and PgAdmin that query the catalog heavily.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_client
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies whether audit messages should be visible to the client. This setting should generally be left disabled but may be useful for debugging or other purposes.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_level
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies the log level that will be used for log entries. This setting is used for regression testing and may also be useful to end users for testing or other purposes.  It is not intended to be used in a production environment as it may leak which statements are being logged to the user.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_parameter
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies that audit logging should include the parameters that were passed with the statement. When parameters are present they will be be included in CSV format after the statement text.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_parameter_max_size
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies, in bytes, the maximum length of variable-length parameters to log.  If 0 (the default), parameters are not checked for size.  If set, when the size of the parameter is longer than the setting, the value in the audit log is replaced with a placeholder. Note that for character types, the length is in bytes for the parameter's encoding, not characters.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_relation
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies whether session audit logging should create a separate log entry for each relation referenced in a SELECT or DML statement. This is a useful shortcut for exhaustive logging without using object audit logging.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_rows
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies whether logging will include the rows retrieved or affected by a statement.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_statement
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters.  Depending on requirements, the full statement text might not be required in the audit log.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.log_statement_once
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters with the first log entry for a statement/substatement combination or with every entry.  Enabling this setting will result in less verbose logging but may make it more difficult to determine the statement that generated a log entry, though the statement/substatement pair along with the process id should suffice to identify the statement text logged with a previous entry.

server_settings.name: pgaudit.role
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies the master role to use for object audit logging.  Multiple audit roles can be defined by granting them to the master role. This allows multiple groups to be in charge of different aspects of audit logging.

server_settings.name: supautils.restrict_extension_versions
server_settings.short_desc: Restrict CREATE/ALTER EXTENSION version specification to superusers
server_settings.extra_desc: off: no restriction; warn: ignore the specified version with a warning and use the default version; error: reject the statement

server_settings.name: supautils.superuser
server_settings.short_desc: Superuser to install extensions in supautils.privileged_extensions as

server_settings.name: vault.getkey_script
server_settings.short_desc: path to script that returns vault root key

server_settings.name: allow_in_place_tablespaces
server_settings.short_desc: Allows tablespaces directly inside pg_tblspc, for testing.

server_settings.name: allow_system_table_mods
server_settings.short_desc: Allows modifications of the structure of system tables.

server_settings.name: backtrace_functions
server_settings.short_desc: Log backtrace for errors in these functions.

server_settings.name: debug_discard_caches
server_settings.short_desc: Aggressively flush system caches for debugging purposes.

server_settings.name: debug_io_direct
server_settings.short_desc: Use direct I/O for file access.

server_settings.name: debug_logical_replication_streaming
server_settings.short_desc: Forces immediate streaming or serialization of changes in large transactions.
server_settings.extra_desc: On the publisher, it allows streaming or serializing each change in logical decoding. On the subscriber, it allows serialization of all changes to files and notifies the parallel apply workers to read and apply them at the end of the transaction.

server_settings.name: debug_parallel_query
server_settings.short_desc: Forces the planner's use parallel query nodes.
server_settings.extra_desc: This can be useful for testing the parallel query infrastructure by forcing the planner to generate plans that contain nodes that perform tuple communication between workers and the main process.

server_settings.name: ignore_checksum_failure
server_settings.short_desc: Continues processing after a checksum failure.
server_settings.extra_desc: Detection of a checksum failure normally causes PostgreSQL to report an error, aborting the current transaction. Setting ignore_checksum_failure to true causes the system to ignore the failure (but still report a warning), and continue processing. This behavior could cause crashes or other serious problems. Only has an effect if checksums are enabled.

server_settings.name: ignore_invalid_pages
server_settings.short_desc: Continues recovery after an invalid pages failure.
server_settings.extra_desc: Detection of WAL records having references to invalid pages during recovery causes PostgreSQL to raise a PANIC-level error, aborting the recovery. Setting "ignore_invalid_pages" to true causes the system to ignore invalid page references in WAL records (but still report a warning), and continue recovery. This behavior may cause crashes, data loss, propagate or hide corruption, or other serious problems. Only has an effect during recovery or in standby mode.

server_settings.name: ignore_system_indexes
server_settings.short_desc: Disables reading from system indexes.
server_settings.extra_desc: It does not prevent updating the indexes, so it is safe to use.  The worst consequence is slowness.

server_settings.name: jit_debugging_support
server_settings.short_desc: Register JIT-compiled functions with debugger.

server_settings.name: jit_dump_bitcode
server_settings.short_desc: Write out LLVM bitcode to facilitate JIT debugging.

server_settings.name: jit_expressions
server_settings.short_desc: Allow JIT compilation of expressions.

server_settings.name: jit_profiling_support
server_settings.short_desc: Register JIT-compiled functions with perf profiler.

server_settings.name: jit_tuple_deforming
server_settings.short_desc: Allow JIT compilation of tuple deforming.

server_settings.name: post_auth_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the amount of time to wait after authentication on connection startup.
server_settings.extra_desc: This allows attaching a debugger to the process.

server_settings.name: pre_auth_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the amount of time to wait before authentication on connection startup.
server_settings.extra_desc: This allows attaching a debugger to the process.

server_settings.name: remove_temp_files_after_crash
server_settings.short_desc: Remove temporary files after backend crash.

server_settings.name: send_abort_for_crash
server_settings.short_desc: Send SIGABRT not SIGQUIT to child processes after backend crash.

server_settings.name: send_abort_for_kill
server_settings.short_desc: Send SIGABRT not SIGKILL to stuck child processes.

server_settings.name: trace_connection_negotiation
server_settings.short_desc: Logs details of pre-authentication connection handshake.

server_settings.name: trace_notify
server_settings.short_desc: Generates debugging output for LISTEN and NOTIFY.

server_settings.name: trace_sort
server_settings.short_desc: Emit information about resource usage in sorting.

server_settings.name: wal_consistency_checking
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the WAL resource managers for which WAL consistency checks are done.
server_settings.extra_desc: Full-page images will be logged for all data blocks and cross-checked against the results of WAL replay.

server_settings.name: zero_damaged_pages
server_settings.short_desc: Continues processing past damaged page headers.
server_settings.extra_desc: Detection of a damaged page header normally causes PostgreSQL to report an error, aborting the current transaction. Setting "zero_damaged_pages" to true causes the system to instead report a warning, zero out the damaged page, and continue processing. This behavior will destroy data, namely all the rows on the damaged page.

server_settings.name: data_sync_retry
server_settings.short_desc: Whether to continue running after a failure to sync data files.

server_settings.name: exit_on_error
server_settings.short_desc: Terminate session on any error.

server_settings.name: recovery_init_sync_method
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the method for synchronizing the data directory before crash recovery.

server_settings.name: restart_after_crash
server_settings.short_desc: Reinitialize server after backend crash.

server_settings.name: deadlock_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the time to wait on a lock before checking for deadlock.

server_settings.name: max_locks_per_transaction
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of locks per transaction.
server_settings.extra_desc: The shared lock table is sized on the assumption that at most "max_locks_per_transaction" objects per server process or prepared transaction will need to be locked at any one time.

server_settings.name: max_pred_locks_per_page
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of predicate-locked tuples per page.
server_settings.extra_desc: If more than this number of tuples on the same page are locked by a connection, those locks are replaced by a page-level lock.

server_settings.name: max_pred_locks_per_relation
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of predicate-locked pages and tuples per relation.
server_settings.extra_desc: If more than this total of pages and tuples in the same relation are locked by a connection, those locks are replaced by a relation-level lock.

server_settings.name: max_pred_locks_per_transaction
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of predicate locks per transaction.
server_settings.extra_desc: The shared predicate lock table is sized on the assumption that at most "max_pred_locks_per_transaction" objects per server process or prepared transaction will need to be locked at any one time.

server_settings.name: block_size
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the size of a disk block.

server_settings.name: data_checksums
server_settings.short_desc: Shows whether data checksums are turned on for this cluster.

server_settings.name: data_directory_mode
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the mode of the data directory.
server_settings.extra_desc: The parameter value is a numeric mode specification in the form accepted by the chmod and umask system calls. (To use the customary octal format the number must start with a 0 (zero).)

server_settings.name: debug_assertions
server_settings.short_desc: Shows whether the running server has assertion checks enabled.

server_settings.name: huge_pages_status
server_settings.short_desc: Indicates the status of huge pages.

server_settings.name: in_hot_standby
server_settings.short_desc: Shows whether hot standby is currently active.

server_settings.name: integer_datetimes
server_settings.short_desc: Shows whether datetimes are integer based.

server_settings.name: max_function_args
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the maximum number of function arguments.

server_settings.name: max_identifier_length
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the maximum identifier length.

server_settings.name: max_index_keys
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the maximum number of index keys.

server_settings.name: segment_size
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the number of pages per disk file.

server_settings.name: server_encoding
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the server (database) character set encoding.

server_settings.name: server_version
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the server version.

server_settings.name: server_version_num
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the server version as an integer.

server_settings.name: shared_memory_size
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the size of the server's main shared memory area (rounded up to the nearest MB).

server_settings.name: shared_memory_size_in_huge_pages
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the number of huge pages needed for the main shared memory area.
server_settings.extra_desc: -1 indicates that the value could not be determined.

server_settings.name: ssl_library
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the name of the SSL library.

server_settings.name: wal_block_size
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the block size in the write ahead log.

server_settings.name: wal_segment_size
server_settings.short_desc: Shows the size of write ahead log segments.

server_settings.name: geqo
server_settings.short_desc: Enables genetic query optimization.
server_settings.extra_desc: This algorithm attempts to do planning without exhaustive searching.

server_settings.name: geqo_effort
server_settings.short_desc: GEQO: effort is used to set the default for other GEQO parameters.

server_settings.name: geqo_generations
server_settings.short_desc: GEQO: number of iterations of the algorithm.
server_settings.extra_desc: Zero selects a suitable default value.

server_settings.name: geqo_pool_size
server_settings.short_desc: GEQO: number of individuals in the population.
server_settings.extra_desc: Zero selects a suitable default value.

server_settings.name: geqo_seed
server_settings.short_desc: GEQO: seed for random path selection.

server_settings.name: geqo_selection_bias
server_settings.short_desc: GEQO: selective pressure within the population.

server_settings.name: geqo_threshold
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the threshold of FROM items beyond which GEQO is used.

server_settings.name: constraint_exclusion
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner to use constraints to optimize queries.
server_settings.extra_desc: Table scans will be skipped if their constraints guarantee that no rows match the query.

server_settings.name: cursor_tuple_fraction
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the fraction of a cursor's rows that will be retrieved.

server_settings.name: default_statistics_target
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the default statistics target.
server_settings.extra_desc: This applies to table columns that have not had a column-specific target set via ALTER TABLE SET STATISTICS.

server_settings.name: from_collapse_limit
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the FROM-list size beyond which subqueries are not collapsed.
server_settings.extra_desc: The planner will merge subqueries into upper queries if the resulting FROM list would have no more than this many items.

server_settings.name: jit
server_settings.short_desc: Allow JIT compilation.

server_settings.name: join_collapse_limit
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the FROM-list size beyond which JOIN constructs are not flattened.
server_settings.extra_desc: The planner will flatten explicit JOIN constructs into lists of FROM items whenever a list of no more than this many items would result.

server_settings.name: plan_cache_mode
server_settings.short_desc: Controls the planner's selection of custom or generic plan.
server_settings.extra_desc: Prepared statements can have custom and generic plans, and the planner will attempt to choose which is better.  This can be set to override the default behavior.

server_settings.name: recursive_worktable_factor
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the average size of a recursive query's working table.

server_settings.name: cpu_index_tuple_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of processing each index entry during an index scan.

server_settings.name: cpu_operator_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of processing each operator or function call.

server_settings.name: cpu_tuple_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of processing each tuple (row).

server_settings.name: effective_cache_size
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's assumption about the total size of the data caches.
server_settings.extra_desc: That is, the total size of the caches (kernel cache and shared buffers) used for PostgreSQL data files. This is measured in disk pages, which are normally 8 kB each.

server_settings.name: jit_above_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Perform JIT compilation if query is more expensive.
server_settings.extra_desc: -1 disables JIT compilation.

server_settings.name: jit_inline_above_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Perform JIT inlining if query is more expensive.
server_settings.extra_desc: -1 disables inlining.

server_settings.name: jit_optimize_above_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Optimize JIT-compiled functions if query is more expensive.
server_settings.extra_desc: -1 disables optimization.

server_settings.name: min_parallel_index_scan_size
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum amount of index data for a parallel scan.
server_settings.extra_desc: If the planner estimates that it will read a number of index pages too small to reach this limit, a parallel scan will not be considered.

server_settings.name: min_parallel_table_scan_size
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum amount of table data for a parallel scan.
server_settings.extra_desc: If the planner estimates that it will read a number of table pages too small to reach this limit, a parallel scan will not be considered.

server_settings.name: parallel_setup_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of starting up worker processes for parallel query.

server_settings.name: parallel_tuple_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of passing each tuple (row) from worker to leader backend.

server_settings.name: random_page_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of a nonsequentially fetched disk page.

server_settings.name: seq_page_cost
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the planner's estimate of the cost of a sequentially fetched disk page.

server_settings.name: enable_async_append
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of async append plans.

server_settings.name: enable_bitmapscan
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of bitmap-scan plans.

server_settings.name: enable_gathermerge
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of gather merge plans.

server_settings.name: enable_group_by_reordering
server_settings.short_desc: Enables reordering of GROUP BY keys.

server_settings.name: enable_hashagg
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of hashed aggregation plans.

server_settings.name: enable_hashjoin
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of hash join plans.

server_settings.name: enable_incremental_sort
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of incremental sort steps.

server_settings.name: enable_indexonlyscan
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of index-only-scan plans.

server_settings.name: enable_indexscan
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of index-scan plans.

server_settings.name: enable_material
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of materialization.

server_settings.name: enable_memoize
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of memoization.

server_settings.name: enable_mergejoin
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of merge join plans.

server_settings.name: enable_nestloop
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of nested-loop join plans.

server_settings.name: enable_parallel_append
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of parallel append plans.

server_settings.name: enable_parallel_hash
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of parallel hash plans.

server_settings.name: enable_partition_pruning
server_settings.short_desc: Enables plan-time and execution-time partition pruning.
server_settings.extra_desc: Allows the query planner and executor to compare partition bounds to conditions in the query to determine which partitions must be scanned.

server_settings.name: enable_partitionwise_aggregate
server_settings.short_desc: Enables partitionwise aggregation and grouping.

server_settings.name: enable_partitionwise_join
server_settings.short_desc: Enables partitionwise join.

server_settings.name: enable_presorted_aggregate
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's ability to produce plans that provide presorted input for ORDER BY / DISTINCT aggregate functions.
server_settings.extra_desc: Allows the query planner to build plans that provide presorted input for aggregate functions with an ORDER BY / DISTINCT clause.  When disabled, implicit sorts are always performed during execution.

server_settings.name: enable_seqscan
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of sequential-scan plans.

server_settings.name: enable_sort
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of explicit sort steps.

server_settings.name: enable_tidscan
server_settings.short_desc: Enables the planner's use of TID scan plans.

server_settings.name: synchronized_standby_slots
server_settings.short_desc: Lists streaming replication standby server replication slot names that logical WAL sender processes will wait for.
server_settings.extra_desc: Logical WAL sender processes will send decoded changes to output plugins only after the specified replication slots have confirmed receiving WAL.

server_settings.name: synchronous_standby_names
server_settings.short_desc: Number of synchronous standbys and list of names of potential synchronous ones.

server_settings.name: max_replication_slots
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of simultaneously defined replication slots.

server_settings.name: max_slot_wal_keep_size
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum WAL size that can be reserved by replication slots.
server_settings.extra_desc: Replication slots will be marked as failed, and segments released for deletion or recycling, if this much space is occupied by WAL on disk.

server_settings.name: max_wal_senders
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of simultaneously running WAL sender processes.

server_settings.name: track_commit_timestamp
server_settings.short_desc: Collects transaction commit time.

server_settings.name: wal_keep_size
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of WAL files held for standby servers.

server_settings.name: wal_sender_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum time to wait for WAL replication.

server_settings.name: hot_standby
server_settings.short_desc: Allows connections and queries during recovery.

server_settings.name: hot_standby_feedback
server_settings.short_desc: Allows feedback from a hot standby to the primary that will avoid query conflicts.

server_settings.name: max_standby_archive_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum delay before canceling queries when a hot standby server is processing archived WAL data.

server_settings.name: max_standby_streaming_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum delay before canceling queries when a hot standby server is processing streamed WAL data.

server_settings.name: primary_slot_name
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the name of the replication slot to use on the sending server.

server_settings.name: recovery_min_apply_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum delay for applying changes during recovery.

server_settings.name: sync_replication_slots
server_settings.short_desc: Enables a physical standby to synchronize logical failover replication slots from the primary server.

server_settings.name: wal_receiver_create_temp_slot
server_settings.short_desc: Sets whether a WAL receiver should create a temporary replication slot if no permanent slot is configured.

server_settings.name: wal_receiver_status_interval
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum interval between WAL receiver status reports to the sending server.

server_settings.name: wal_receiver_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum wait time to receive data from the sending server.

server_settings.name: wal_retrieve_retry_interval
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the time to wait before retrying to retrieve WAL after a failed attempt.

server_settings.name: max_logical_replication_workers
server_settings.short_desc: Maximum number of logical replication worker processes.

server_settings.name: max_parallel_apply_workers_per_subscription
server_settings.short_desc: Maximum number of parallel apply workers per subscription.

server_settings.name: max_sync_workers_per_subscription
server_settings.short_desc: Maximum number of table synchronization workers per subscription.

server_settings.name: cluster_name
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the name of the cluster, which is included in the process title.

server_settings.name: update_process_title
server_settings.short_desc: Updates the process title to show the active SQL command.
server_settings.extra_desc: Enables updating of the process title every time a new SQL command is received by the server.

server_settings.name: application_name
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the application name to be reported in statistics and logs.

server_settings.name: debug_pretty_print
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Indents parse and plan tree displays.

server_settings.name: debug_print_parse
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs each query's parse tree.

server_settings.name: debug_print_plan
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs each query's execution plan.

server_settings.name: debug_print_rewritten
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs each query's rewritten parse tree.

server_settings.name: log_autovacuum_min_duration
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum execution time above which autovacuum actions will be logged.
server_settings.extra_desc: Zero prints all actions. -1 turns autovacuum logging off.

server_settings.name: log_checkpoints
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs each checkpoint.

server_settings.name: log_connections
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs each successful connection.

server_settings.name: log_disconnections
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs end of a session, including duration.

server_settings.name: log_duration
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs the duration of each completed SQL statement.

server_settings.name: log_error_verbosity
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the verbosity of logged messages.

server_settings.name: log_hostname
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs the host name in the connection logs.
server_settings.extra_desc: By default, connection logs only show the IP address of the connecting host. If you want them to show the host name you can turn this on, but depending on your host name resolution setup it might impose a non-negligible performance penalty.

server_settings.name: log_line_prefix
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Controls information prefixed to each log line.
server_settings.extra_desc: If blank, no prefix is used.

server_settings.name: log_lock_waits
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs long lock waits.

server_settings.name: log_parameter_max_length
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum length in bytes of data logged for bind parameter values when logging statements.
server_settings.extra_desc: -1 to print values in full.

server_settings.name: log_parameter_max_length_on_error
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum length in bytes of data logged for bind parameter values when logging statements, on error.
server_settings.extra_desc: -1 to print values in full.

server_settings.name: log_recovery_conflict_waits
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs standby recovery conflict waits.

server_settings.name: log_replication_commands
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Logs each replication command.

server_settings.name: log_statement
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the type of statements logged.

server_settings.name: log_temp_files
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Log the use of temporary files larger than this number of kilobytes.
server_settings.extra_desc: Zero logs all files. The default is -1 (turning this feature off).

server_settings.name: log_timezone
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / What to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the time zone to use in log messages.

server_settings.name: log_min_duration_sample
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / When to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum execution time above which a sample of statements will be logged. Sampling is determined by log_statement_sample_rate.
server_settings.extra_desc: Zero logs a sample of all queries. -1 turns this feature off.

server_settings.name: log_min_duration_statement
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / When to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum execution time above which all statements will be logged.
server_settings.extra_desc: Zero prints all queries. -1 turns this feature off.

server_settings.name: log_min_error_statement
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / When to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Causes all statements generating error at or above this level to be logged.
server_settings.extra_desc: Each level includes all the levels that follow it. The later the level, the fewer messages are sent.

server_settings.name: log_min_messages
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / When to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the message levels that are logged.
server_settings.extra_desc: Each level includes all the levels that follow it. The later the level, the fewer messages are sent.

server_settings.name: log_startup_progress_interval
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / When to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Time between progress updates for long-running startup operations.
server_settings.extra_desc: 0 turns this feature off.

server_settings.name: log_statement_sample_rate
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / When to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Fraction of statements exceeding "log_min_duration_sample" to be logged.
server_settings.extra_desc: Use a value between 0.0 (never log) and 1.0 (always log).

server_settings.name: log_transaction_sample_rate
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / When to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the fraction of transactions from which to log all statements.
server_settings.extra_desc: Use a value between 0.0 (never log) and 1.0 (log all statements for all transactions).

server_settings.name: event_source
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the application name used to identify PostgreSQL messages in the event log.

server_settings.name: log_destination
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the destination for server log output.
server_settings.extra_desc: Valid values are combinations of "stderr", "syslog", "csvlog", "jsonlog", and "eventlog", depending on the platform.

server_settings.name: log_file_mode
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the file permissions for log files.
server_settings.extra_desc: The parameter value is expected to be a numeric mode specification in the form accepted by the chmod and umask system calls. (To use the customary octal format the number must start with a 0 (zero).)

server_settings.name: log_rotation_age
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the amount of time to wait before forcing log file rotation.

server_settings.name: log_rotation_size
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum size a log file can reach before being rotated.

server_settings.name: log_truncate_on_rotation
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Truncate existing log files of same name during log rotation.

server_settings.name: logging_collector
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Start a subprocess to capture stderr, csvlog and/or jsonlog into log files.

server_settings.name: syslog_facility
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the syslog "facility" to be used when syslog enabled.

server_settings.name: syslog_ident
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the program name used to identify PostgreSQL messages in syslog.

server_settings.name: syslog_sequence_numbers
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Add sequence number to syslog messages to avoid duplicate suppression.

server_settings.name: syslog_split_messages
server_settings.category: Reporting and Logging / Where to Log
server_settings.short_desc: Split messages sent to syslog by lines and to fit into 1024 bytes.

server_settings.name: backend_flush_after
server_settings.short_desc: Number of pages after which previously performed writes are flushed to disk.

server_settings.name: effective_io_concurrency
server_settings.short_desc: Number of simultaneous requests that can be handled efficiently by the disk subsystem.

server_settings.name: io_combine_limit
server_settings.short_desc: Limit on the size of data reads and writes.

server_settings.name: maintenance_io_concurrency
server_settings.short_desc: A variant of "effective_io_concurrency" that is used for maintenance work.

server_settings.name: max_parallel_maintenance_workers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of parallel processes per maintenance operation.

server_settings.name: max_parallel_workers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of parallel workers that can be active at one time.

server_settings.name: max_parallel_workers_per_gather
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of parallel processes per executor node.

server_settings.name: max_worker_processes
server_settings.short_desc: Maximum number of concurrent worker processes.

server_settings.name: parallel_leader_participation
server_settings.short_desc: Controls whether Gather and Gather Merge also run subplans.
server_settings.extra_desc: Should gather nodes also run subplans or just gather tuples?

server_settings.name: bgwriter_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Background writer sleep time between rounds.

server_settings.name: bgwriter_flush_after
server_settings.short_desc: Number of pages after which previously performed writes are flushed to disk.

server_settings.name: bgwriter_lru_maxpages
server_settings.short_desc: Background writer maximum number of LRU pages to flush per round.

server_settings.name: bgwriter_lru_multiplier
server_settings.short_desc: Multiple of the average buffer usage to free per round.

server_settings.name: vacuum_cost_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Vacuum cost delay in milliseconds.

server_settings.name: vacuum_cost_limit
server_settings.short_desc: Vacuum cost amount available before napping.

server_settings.name: vacuum_cost_page_dirty
server_settings.short_desc: Vacuum cost for a page dirtied by vacuum.

server_settings.name: vacuum_cost_page_hit
server_settings.short_desc: Vacuum cost for a page found in the buffer cache.

server_settings.name: vacuum_cost_page_miss
server_settings.short_desc: Vacuum cost for a page not found in the buffer cache.

server_settings.name: max_notify_queue_pages
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of allocated pages for NOTIFY / LISTEN queue.

server_settings.name: temp_file_limit
server_settings.short_desc: Limits the total size of all temporary files used by each process.
server_settings.extra_desc: -1 means no limit.

server_settings.name: max_files_per_process
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of simultaneously open files for each server process.

server_settings.name: autovacuum_work_mem
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum memory to be used by each autovacuum worker process.

server_settings.name: commit_timestamp_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of the dedicated buffer pool used for the commit timestamp cache.
server_settings.extra_desc: Specify 0 to have this value determined as a fraction of shared_buffers.

server_settings.name: dynamic_shared_memory_type
server_settings.short_desc: Selects the dynamic shared memory implementation used.

server_settings.name: hash_mem_multiplier
server_settings.short_desc: Multiple of "work_mem" to use for hash tables.

server_settings.name: huge_page_size
server_settings.short_desc: The size of huge page that should be requested.

server_settings.name: huge_pages
server_settings.short_desc: Use of huge pages on Linux or Windows.

server_settings.name: logical_decoding_work_mem
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum memory to be used for logical decoding.
server_settings.extra_desc: This much memory can be used by each internal reorder buffer before spilling to disk.

server_settings.name: maintenance_work_mem
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum memory to be used for maintenance operations.
server_settings.extra_desc: This includes operations such as VACUUM and CREATE INDEX.

server_settings.name: max_prepared_transactions
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of simultaneously prepared transactions.

server_settings.name: max_stack_depth
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum stack depth, in kilobytes.

server_settings.name: min_dynamic_shared_memory
server_settings.short_desc: Amount of dynamic shared memory reserved at startup.

server_settings.name: multixact_member_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of the dedicated buffer pool used for the MultiXact member cache.

server_settings.name: multixact_offset_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of the dedicated buffer pool used for the MultiXact offset cache.

server_settings.name: notify_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of the dedicated buffer pool used for the LISTEN/NOTIFY message cache.

server_settings.name: serializable_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of the dedicated buffer pool used for the serializable transaction cache.

server_settings.name: shared_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the number of shared memory buffers used by the server.

server_settings.name: shared_memory_type
server_settings.short_desc: Selects the shared memory implementation used for the main shared memory region.

server_settings.name: subtransaction_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of the dedicated buffer pool used for the subtransaction cache.
server_settings.extra_desc: Specify 0 to have this value determined as a fraction of shared_buffers.

server_settings.name: temp_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum number of temporary buffers used by each session.

server_settings.name: transaction_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size of the dedicated buffer pool used for the transaction status cache.
server_settings.extra_desc: Specify 0 to have this value determined as a fraction of shared_buffers.

server_settings.name: vacuum_buffer_usage_limit
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the buffer pool size for VACUUM, ANALYZE, and autovacuum.

server_settings.name: work_mem
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum memory to be used for query workspaces.
server_settings.extra_desc: This much memory can be used by each internal sort operation and hash table before switching to temporary disk files.

server_settings.name: stats_fetch_consistency
server_settings.category: Statistics / Cumulative Query and Index Statistics
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the consistency of accesses to statistics data.

server_settings.name: track_activities
server_settings.category: Statistics / Cumulative Query and Index Statistics
server_settings.short_desc: Collects information about executing commands.
server_settings.extra_desc: Enables the collection of information on the currently executing command of each session, along with the time at which that command began execution.

server_settings.name: track_activity_query_size
server_settings.category: Statistics / Cumulative Query and Index Statistics
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the size reserved for pg_stat_activity.query, in bytes.

server_settings.name: track_counts
server_settings.category: Statistics / Cumulative Query and Index Statistics
server_settings.short_desc: Collects statistics on database activity.

server_settings.name: track_functions
server_settings.category: Statistics / Cumulative Query and Index Statistics
server_settings.short_desc: Collects function-level statistics on database activity.

server_settings.name: track_io_timing
server_settings.category: Statistics / Cumulative Query and Index Statistics
server_settings.short_desc: Collects timing statistics for database I/O activity.

server_settings.name: track_wal_io_timing
server_settings.category: Statistics / Cumulative Query and Index Statistics
server_settings.short_desc: Collects timing statistics for WAL I/O activity.

server_settings.name: compute_query_id
server_settings.short_desc: Enables in-core computation of query identifiers.

server_settings.name: log_executor_stats
server_settings.short_desc: Writes executor performance statistics to the server log.

server_settings.name: log_parser_stats
server_settings.short_desc: Writes parser performance statistics to the server log.

server_settings.name: log_planner_stats
server_settings.short_desc: Writes planner performance statistics to the server log.

server_settings.name: log_statement_stats
server_settings.short_desc: Writes cumulative performance statistics to the server log.

server_settings.name: allow_alter_system
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Other Platforms and Clients
server_settings.short_desc: Allows running the ALTER SYSTEM command.
server_settings.extra_desc: Can be set to off for environments where global configuration changes should be made using a different method.

server_settings.name: transform_null_equals
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Other Platforms and Clients
server_settings.short_desc: Treats "expr=NULL" as "expr IS NULL".
server_settings.extra_desc: When turned on, expressions of the form expr = NULL (or NULL = expr) are treated as expr IS NULL, that is, they return true if expr evaluates to the null value, and false otherwise. The correct behavior of expr = NULL is to always return null (unknown).

server_settings.name: array_nulls
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Previous PostgreSQL Versions
server_settings.short_desc: Enable input of NULL elements in arrays.
server_settings.extra_desc: When turned on, unquoted NULL in an array input value means a null value; otherwise it is taken literally.

server_settings.name: backslash_quote
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Previous PostgreSQL Versions
server_settings.short_desc: Sets whether "\'" is allowed in string literals.

server_settings.name: escape_string_warning
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Previous PostgreSQL Versions
server_settings.short_desc: Warn about backslash escapes in ordinary string literals.

server_settings.name: lo_compat_privileges
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Previous PostgreSQL Versions
server_settings.short_desc: Enables backward compatibility mode for privilege checks on large objects.
server_settings.extra_desc: Skips privilege checks when reading or modifying large objects, for compatibility with PostgreSQL releases prior to 9.0.

server_settings.name: quote_all_identifiers
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Previous PostgreSQL Versions
server_settings.short_desc: When generating SQL fragments, quote all identifiers.

server_settings.name: standard_conforming_strings
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Previous PostgreSQL Versions
server_settings.short_desc: Causes '...' strings to treat backslashes literally.

server_settings.name: synchronize_seqscans
server_settings.category: Version and Platform Compatibility / Previous PostgreSQL Versions
server_settings.short_desc: Enable synchronized sequential scans.

server_settings.name: archive_cleanup_command
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the shell command that will be executed at every restart point.

server_settings.name: recovery_end_command
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the shell command that will be executed once at the end of recovery.

server_settings.name: restore_command
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the shell command that will be called to retrieve an archived WAL file.

server_settings.name: archive_command
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the shell command that will be called to archive a WAL file.
server_settings.extra_desc: This is used only if "archive_library" is not set.

server_settings.name: archive_library
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the library that will be called to archive a WAL file.
server_settings.extra_desc: An empty string indicates that "archive_command" should be used.

server_settings.name: archive_mode
server_settings.short_desc: Allows archiving of WAL files using "archive_command".

server_settings.name: archive_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the amount of time to wait before forcing a switch to the next WAL file.

server_settings.name: checkpoint_completion_target
server_settings.short_desc: Time spent flushing dirty buffers during checkpoint, as fraction of checkpoint interval.

server_settings.name: checkpoint_flush_after
server_settings.short_desc: Number of pages after which previously performed writes are flushed to disk.

server_settings.name: checkpoint_timeout
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum time between automatic WAL checkpoints.

server_settings.name: checkpoint_warning
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the maximum time before warning if checkpoints triggered by WAL volume happen too frequently.
server_settings.extra_desc: Write a message to the server log if checkpoints caused by the filling of WAL segment files happen more frequently than this amount of time. Zero turns off the warning.

server_settings.name: max_wal_size
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the WAL size that triggers a checkpoint.

server_settings.name: min_wal_size
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum size to shrink the WAL to.

server_settings.name: recovery_prefetch
server_settings.short_desc: Prefetch referenced blocks during recovery.
server_settings.extra_desc: Look ahead in the WAL to find references to uncached data.

server_settings.name: wal_decode_buffer_size
server_settings.short_desc: Buffer size for reading ahead in the WAL during recovery.
server_settings.extra_desc: Maximum distance to read ahead in the WAL to prefetch referenced data blocks.

server_settings.name: recovery_target
server_settings.short_desc: Set to "immediate" to end recovery as soon as a consistent state is reached.

server_settings.name: recovery_target_action
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the action to perform upon reaching the recovery target.

server_settings.name: recovery_target_inclusive
server_settings.short_desc: Sets whether to include or exclude transaction with recovery target.

server_settings.name: recovery_target_lsn
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the LSN of the write-ahead log location up to which recovery will proceed.

server_settings.name: recovery_target_name
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the named restore point up to which recovery will proceed.

server_settings.name: recovery_target_time
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the time stamp up to which recovery will proceed.

server_settings.name: recovery_target_timeline
server_settings.short_desc: Specifies the timeline to recover into.

server_settings.name: recovery_target_xid
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the transaction ID up to which recovery will proceed.

server_settings.name: commit_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the delay in microseconds between transaction commit and flushing WAL to disk.

server_settings.name: commit_siblings
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the minimum number of concurrent open transactions required before performing "commit_delay".

server_settings.name: fsync
server_settings.short_desc: Forces synchronization of updates to disk.
server_settings.extra_desc: The server will use the fsync() system call in several places to make sure that updates are physically written to disk. This ensures that a database cluster will recover to a consistent state after an operating system or hardware crash.

server_settings.name: full_page_writes
server_settings.short_desc: Writes full pages to WAL when first modified after a checkpoint.
server_settings.extra_desc: A page write in process during an operating system crash might be only partially written to disk.  During recovery, the row changes stored in WAL are not enough to recover.  This option writes pages when first modified after a checkpoint to WAL so full recovery is possible.

server_settings.name: synchronous_commit
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the current transaction's synchronization level.

server_settings.name: wal_buffers
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the number of disk-page buffers in shared memory for WAL.
server_settings.extra_desc: Specify -1 to have this value determined as a fraction of shared_buffers.

server_settings.name: wal_compression
server_settings.short_desc: Compresses full-page writes written in WAL file with specified method.

server_settings.name: wal_init_zero
server_settings.short_desc: Writes zeroes to new WAL files before first use.

server_settings.name: wal_level
server_settings.short_desc: Sets the level of information written to the WAL.

server_settings.name: wal_log_hints
server_settings.short_desc: Writes full pages to WAL when first modified after a checkpoint, even for a non-critical modification.

server_settings.name: wal_recycle
server_settings.short_desc: Recycles WAL files by renaming them.

server_settings.name: wal_skip_threshold
server_settings.short_desc: Minimum size of new file to fsync instead of writing WAL.

server_settings.name: wal_sync_method
server_settings.short_desc: Selects the method used for forcing WAL updates to disk.

server_settings.name: wal_writer_delay
server_settings.short_desc: Time between WAL flushes performed in the WAL writer.

server_settings.name: wal_writer_flush_after
server_settings.short_desc: Amount of WAL written out by WAL writer that triggers a flush.

server_settings.name: summarize_wal
server_settings.short_desc: Starts the WAL summarizer process to enable incremental backup.

server_settings.name: wal_summary_keep_time
server_settings.short_desc: Time for which WAL summary files should be kept.

DECLARE
  cmd record;
BEGIN
  FOR cmd IN SELECT * FROM pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands()
  LOOP
    IF cmd.command_tag IN (
      'CREATE SCHEMA', 'ALTER SCHEMA'
    , 'CREATE TABLE', 'CREATE TABLE AS', 'SELECT INTO', 'ALTER TABLE'
    , 'CREATE FOREIGN TABLE', 'ALTER FOREIGN TABLE'
    , 'CREATE VIEW', 'ALTER VIEW'
    , 'CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW', 'ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW'
    , 'CREATE FUNCTION', 'ALTER FUNCTION'
    , 'CREATE TRIGGER'
    , 'CREATE TYPE', 'ALTER TYPE'
    , 'CREATE RULE'
    , 'COMMENT'
    )
    -- don't notify in case of CREATE TEMP table or other objects created on pg_temp
    AND cmd.schema_name is distinct from 'pg_temp'
    THEN
      NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END;

DECLARE
  obj record;
BEGIN
  FOR obj IN SELECT * FROM pg_event_trigger_dropped_objects()
  LOOP
    IF obj.object_type IN (
      'schema'
    , 'table'
    , 'foreign table'
    , 'view'
    , 'materialized view'
    , 'function'
    , 'trigger'
    , 'type'
    , 'rule'
    )
    AND obj.is_temporary IS false -- no pg_temp objects
    THEN
      NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END;

begin
  return query
  with candidates as (
    select contribution.id
    from public.data_contributions contribution
    where contribution.status in ('pending', 'failed', 'processing')
      and case
        when contribution.status = 'processing' then contribution.lease_expires_at
        else contribution.available_at
      end <= now()
      and contribution.retention_until > now()
    order by
      case
        when contribution.status = 'processing' then contribution.lease_expires_at
        else contribution.available_at
      end,
      contribution.occurred_at,
      contribution.id
    for update skip locked
    limit greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_limit, 25), 250))
  )
  update public.data_contributions contribution
  set status = 'processing',
      attempt_count = contribution.attempt_count + 1,
      lease_expires_at = now() + make_interval(secs => greatest(30, least(coalesce(p_lease_seconds, 300), 3600))),
      updated_at = now()
  from candidates
  where contribution.id = candidates.id
  returning contribution.*;
end;

declare
  v_limit integer := greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_limit, 100), 2000));
  v_lease_seconds integer := greatest(30, least(coalesce(p_lease_seconds, 120), 3600));
  v_shard_count integer := greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_shard_count, 1), 256));
  v_shard_index integer := greatest(0, least(coalesce(p_shard_index, 0), greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_shard_count, 1), 256)) - 1));
  v_worker_id text := left(coalesce(nullif(trim(p_worker_id), ''), 'gateway-reconciler'), 200);
begin
  return query
  with candidates as (
    select op.id
    from public.gateway_async_operations op
    where op.kind = p_kind
      and op.billed_at is null
      and (op.next_reconcile_at is null or op.next_reconcile_at <= now())
      and (
        op.reconcile_locked_at is null
        or op.reconcile_locked_at < now() - make_interval(secs => v_lease_seconds)
      )
      and (
        p_statuses is null
        or coalesce(op.status, '') = any(p_statuses)
      )
      and not (op.kind = 'batch' and op.meta->>'resource' = 'file')
      and (
        v_shard_count = 1
        or mod(
          mod(hashtextextended(op.workspace_id::text || ':' || op.internal_id, 0), v_shard_count::bigint)
            + v_shard_count::bigint,
          v_shard_count::bigint
        ) = v_shard_index::bigint
      )
    order by op.next_reconcile_at asc nulls first, op.updated_at asc
    limit v_limit
    for update skip locked
  ),
  claimed as (
    update public.gateway_async_operations op
    set
      reconcile_locked_at = now(),
      reconcile_locked_by = v_worker_id,
      reconcile_attempts = op.reconcile_attempts + 1,
      updated_at = now()
    from candidates
    where op.id = candidates.id
    returning op.*
  )
  select
    claimed.workspace_id,
    claimed.kind,
    claimed.internal_id,
    claimed.request_id,
    claimed.session_id,
    claimed.app_id,
    claimed.provider,
    claimed.native_id,
    claimed.model,
    claimed.status,
    claimed.meta,
    claimed.billed_at,
    claimed.next_reconcile_at,
    claimed.reconcile_attempts,
    claimed.reconcile_locked_at,
    claimed.reconcile_locked_by,
    claimed.last_reconcile_error,
    claimed.created_at,
    claimed.updated_at
  from claimed
  order by claimed.next_reconcile_at asc nulls first, claimed.updated_at asc;
end;

with current_models as (
    select
      model.provider_id,
      model.model_id,
      coalesce(model.model_details, '{}'::jsonb) as model_details,
      model.pricing_details
    from jsonb_to_recordset(coalesce(p_current_models, '[]'::jsonb)) as model(
      provider_id text,
      model_id text,
      model_details jsonb,
      pricing_details jsonb
    )
    where model.provider_id = any(coalesce(p_provider_ids, array[]::text[]))
  ),
  providers as (
    select distinct provider_id
    from unnest(coalesce(p_provider_ids, array[]::text[])) as provider_id
  ),
  existing_models as (
    select seen.provider_id, seen.model_id, seen.model_details, seen.pricing_details
    from public.model_discovery_seen_models as seen
    join providers using (provider_id)
  ),
  provider_diffs as (
    select
      provider.provider_id,
      (select count(*) from existing_models old where old.provider_id = provider.provider_id) as previous_count,
      (select count(*) from current_models current where current.provider_id = provider.provider_id) as current_count,
      coalesce((
        select jsonb_agg(current.model_id order by current.model_id)
        from current_models current
        where current.provider_id = provider.provider_id
          and not exists (
            select 1 from existing_models old
            where old.provider_id = current.provider_id and old.model_id = current.model_id
          )
      ), '[]'::jsonb) as added,
      coalesce((
        select jsonb_agg(old.model_id order by old.model_id)
        from existing_models old
        where old.provider_id = provider.provider_id
          and not exists (
            select 1 from current_models current
            where current.provider_id = old.provider_id and current.model_id = old.model_id
          )
      ), '[]'::jsonb) as removed
    from providers provider
  ),
  changed_snapshots as (
    select old.provider_id, old.model_id, old.model_details, old.pricing_details
    from existing_models old
    join current_models current using (provider_id, model_id)
    where old.provider_id = any(coalesce(p_snapshot_provider_ids, array[]::text[]))
      and (
        old.model_details is distinct from current.model_details
        or old.pricing_details is distinct from current.pricing_details
      )
  ),
  snapshot_baselines as (
    select distinct old.provider_id
    from existing_models old
    where old.provider_id = any(coalesce(p_snapshot_provider_ids, array[]::text[]))
      and (old.pricing_details is not null or old.model_details <> '{}'::jsonb)
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'providers', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'provider_id', provider_id,
        'previous_count', previous_count,
        'current_count', current_count,
        'added', added,
        'removed', removed
      ) order by provider_id)
      from provider_diffs
    ), '[]'::jsonb),
    'changed_snapshots', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'provider_id', provider_id,
        'model_id', model_id,
        'model_details', model_details,
        'pricing_details', pricing_details
      ) order by provider_id, model_id)
      from changed_snapshots
    ), '[]'::jsonb),
    'snapshot_baseline_provider_ids', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(provider_id order by provider_id) from snapshot_baselines
    ), '[]'::jsonb)
  );

declare
  confirmed jsonb := '[]'::jsonb;
begin
  -- A returning model cancels its pending deletion signal.
  delete from public.model_discovery_issue_signals signal
  where signal.action = 'delete'
    and signal.provider_id = any(coalesce(p_successful_provider_ids, array[]::text[]))
    and exists (
      select 1
      from public.model_discovery_seen_models seen
      where seen.provider_id = signal.provider_id
        and seen.model_id = signal.model_id
    );

  -- Existing absent candidates have now survived another successful sweep.
  update public.model_discovery_issue_signals signal
  set
    consecutive_sweeps = signal.consecutive_sweeps + 1,
    last_observed_at = now(),
    last_observed_run_id = p_run_id
  where signal.action = 'delete'
    and signal.emitted_at is null
    and signal.provider_id = any(coalesce(p_successful_provider_ids, array[]::text[]))
    and signal.last_observed_run_id is distinct from p_run_id
    and not exists (
      select 1
      from public.model_discovery_seen_models seen
      where seen.provider_id = signal.provider_id
        and seen.model_id = signal.model_id
    );

  -- New deletion candidates begin at one observed sweep. Other actions are
  -- returned immediately and do not require confirmation.
  insert into public.model_discovery_issue_signals (
    source,
    provider_id,
    action,
    model_id,
    entry,
    consecutive_sweeps,
    first_observed_at,
    last_observed_at,
    last_observed_run_id
  )
  select
    raw.value ->> 'source',
    raw.value ->> 'providerId',
    raw.value ->> 'action',
    raw.value ->> 'modelId',
    raw.value,
    1,
    now(),
    now(),
    p_run_id
  from jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(p_entries, '[]'::jsonb)) raw(value)
  where raw.value ->> 'action' = 'delete'
    and raw.value ->> 'providerId' = any(coalesce(p_successful_provider_ids, array[]::text[]))
  on conflict (source, provider_id, action, model_id) do update set
    entry = excluded.entry,
    last_observed_at = excluded.last_observed_at,
    last_observed_run_id = excluded.last_observed_run_id;

  with immediate_entries as (
    select value as entry
    from jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(p_entries, '[]'::jsonb))
    where value ->> 'action' <> 'delete'
  ), confirmed_deletions as (
    select signal.entry
    from public.model_discovery_issue_signals signal
    where signal.action = 'delete'
      and signal.emitted_at is null
      and signal.consecutive_sweeps >= 2
      and signal.provider_id = any(coalesce(p_successful_provider_ids, array[]::text[]))
  ), all_confirmed as (
    select entry from immediate_entries
    union all
    select entry from confirmed_deletions
  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(entry), '[]'::jsonb)
  into confirmed
  from all_confirmed;

  return confirmed;
end;

begin
  return query
  with candidates as (
    select event.id
    from public.gateway_provider_events event
    where event.provider = any(p_providers)
      and event.processed_at is null
      and event.dead_lettered_at is null
      and (event.next_attempt_at is null or event.next_attempt_at <= now())
      and (
        event.replay_locked_at is null
        or event.replay_locked_at < now() - make_interval(secs => greatest(30, least(coalesce(p_lease_seconds, 120), 3600)))
      )
    order by event.created_at asc
    for update skip locked
    limit greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_limit, 100), 500))
  )
  update public.gateway_provider_events event
  set replay_locked_at = now(),
      replay_locked_by = left(coalesce(nullif(trim(p_worker_id), ''), 'batch-provider-event-replay'), 200),
      updated_at = now()
  from candidates
  where event.id = candidates.id
  returning event.*;

function_analysis.source_code:
begin
  if p_group_by not in ('preset_id', 'test_run_id', 'metadata') then
    raise exception 'invalid feedback summary grouping' using errcode = '22023';
  end if;
  if p_group_by = 'metadata'
     and (p_metadata_key is null or p_metadata_key !~ '^[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$') then
    raise exception 'valid metadata key required for metadata grouping' using errcode = '22023';
  end if;
  if jsonb_typeof(coalesce(p_metadata_filters, '{}'::jsonb)) <> 'object' then
    raise exception 'metadata filters must be a JSON object' using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  return query
  with filtered as (
    select
      case p_group_by
        when 'preset_id' then feedback.preset_id::text
        when 'test_run_id' then feedback.test_run_id::text
        when 'metadata' then feedback.metadata_dimensions ->> p_metadata_key
      end as summary_group,
      feedback.rating,
      feedback.score,
      feedback.created_at
    from public.gateway_feedback as feedback
    where feedback.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
      and (feedback.preset_id is null or feedback.preset_id = any(coalesce(p_visible_preset_ids, '{}'::uuid[])))
      and (p_request_id is null or feedback.request_id = p_request_id)
      and (p_session_id is null or feedback.session_id = p_session_id)
      and (p_preset_id is null or feedback.preset_id = p_preset_id)
      and (p_test_run_id is null or feedback.test_run_id = p_test_run_id)
      and (p_created_since is null or feedback.created_at >= p_created_since)
      and (p_created_until is null or feedback.created_at <= p_created_until)
      and feedback.metadata_dimensions @> coalesce(p_metadata_filters, '{}'::jsonb)
  ),
  grouped as (
    select summary_group,
      count(*) as feedback_count,
      count(*) filter (where rating in ('thumbs_up', 'correct')) as positive_count,
      count(*) filter (where rating in ('thumbs_down', 'incorrect', 'unsafe')) as negative_count,
      count(*) filter (where rating = 'partly_correct') as partial_count,
      avg(score) filter (where score is not null) as mean_score,
      max(created_at) as latest_feedback_at
    from filtered
    where summary_group is not null and summary_group <> ''
    group by summary_group
  ),
  rating_counts as (
    select summary_group, coalesce(rating, 'unrated') as rating_key, count(*) as rating_count
    from filtered
    where summary_group is not null and summary_group <> ''
    group by summary_group, coalesce(rating, 'unrated')
  ),
  rating_totals as (
    select summary_group, jsonb_object_agg(rating_key, rating_count) as rating_map
    from rating_counts group by summary_group
  )
  select grouped.summary_group, grouped.feedback_count, grouped.positive_count,
    grouped.negative_count, grouped.partial_count, grouped.mean_score,
    coalesce(rating_totals.rating_map, '{}'::jsonb), grouped.latest_feedback_at
  from grouped left join rating_totals using (summary_group)
  order by grouped.latest_feedback_at desc, grouped.summary_group asc
  limit greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_limit, 5000), 10000));
end;

function_analysis.source_code:
with params as (
		select greatest(1, hours_window) as hours_window
	),
	bounds as (
		select
			now() at time zone 'utc' as window_end,
			(now() at time zone 'utc') - (p.hours_window || ' hours')::interval as window_start,
			p.hours_window
		from params p
	),
	scoped_requests as (
		select
			gr.success,
			gr.error_code,
			gr.usage,
			gr.created_at
		from gateway_requests gr
		cross join bounds b
		where gr.created_at >= b.window_start
			and gr.created_at < b.window_end
	)
	select
		b.window_start,
		b.window_end,
		b.hours_window as timeframe_hours,
		count(sr.*) as total_requests,
		case
			when count(sr.*) = 0 then null
			else round(
				(
					100.0 * count(*) filter (
						where coalesce(sr.success, false) or (sr.error_code ilike 'user:%')
					)::double precision
					/ greatest(count(sr.*), 1)::double precision
				)::numeric,
				4
			)::double precision
		end as uptime_pct,
		count(*) filter (
			where coalesce(sr.success, false) or (sr.error_code ilike 'user:%')
		) as uptime_events,
		coalesce(
			sum(
				case
					when jsonb_typeof(sr.usage -> 'total_tokens') = 'number' then
						(sr.usage ->> 'total_tokens')::double precision
					else 0::double precision
				end
			),
			0::double precision
		) as total_tokens
	from bounds b
	left join scoped_requests sr on true
	group by b.window_start, b.window_end, b.hours_window;

function_analysis.arguments: p_workspace_id uuid, p_key_id uuid, p_batch_id text, p_provider text, p_rows jsonb
function_analysis.source_code:
declare
  v_inserted integer := 0;
begin
  if p_workspace_id is null or p_key_id is null or coalesce(trim(p_batch_id), '') = '' then
    raise exception 'invalid_batch_key_usage_identity';
  end if;
  if not exists (
    select 1 from public.keys
    where id = p_key_id and workspace_id = p_workspace_id
  ) then
    raise exception 'batch_key_not_owned_by_workspace';
  end if;
  if jsonb_typeof(p_rows) <> 'array' then
    raise exception 'invalid_batch_key_usage_rows';
  end if;

  delete from public.gateway_requests gr
  where gr.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
    and gr.key_id = p_key_id
    and gr.request_id like 'batch_hold_usage:%'
    and exists (
      select 1
      from public.gateway_wallet_reservations reservation
      where reservation.workspace_id = p_workspace_id
        and reservation.key_id = p_key_id
        and reservation.capture_ref_id = p_batch_id
        and reservation.status = 'captured'
        and gr.request_id like 'batch_hold_usage:' || reservation.reservation_id || ':%'
    );

  with source_rows as (
    select
      coalesce(nullif(trim(row ->> 'custom_id'), ''), ordinality::text) as custom_id,
      coalesce(nullif(trim(row ->> 'endpoint'), ''), 'batch') as endpoint,
      coalesce(nullif(trim(row ->> 'model'), ''), 'batch/unknown') as model,
      greatest(0, coalesce((row ->> 'cost_nanos')::bigint, 0)) as cost_nanos,
      case when jsonb_typeof(row -> 'usage') = 'object' then row -> 'usage' else '{}'::jsonb end as usage
    from jsonb_array_elements(p_rows) with ordinality as entries(row, ordinality)
  ), claimed_rows as (
    insert into public.gateway_batch_key_usage_records (
      workspace_id, batch_id, custom_id, key_id, provider, endpoint, model, cost_nanos, usage
    )
    select
      p_workspace_id, p_batch_id, source.custom_id, p_key_id,
      nullif(trim(coalesce(p_provider, '')), ''), source.endpoint,
      source.model, source.cost_nanos, source.usage
    from source_rows source
    on conflict (workspace_id, batch_id, custom_id) do nothing
    returning custom_id, provider, endpoint, model, cost_nanos, usage
  )
  insert into public.gateway_requests (
    workspace_id, request_id, endpoint, model_id, provider,
    status_code, success, usage, cost_nanos, currency, key_id
  )
  select
    p_workspace_id,
    'batch_usage:' || p_batch_id || ':' || claimed.custom_id,
    claimed.endpoint,
    claimed.model,
    claimed.provider,
    200,
    true,
    claimed.usage,
    claimed.cost_nanos,
    'USD',
    p_key_id
  from claimed_rows claimed;
  get diagnostics v_inserted = row_count;

  update public.gateway_wallet_reservations
  set key_usage_recorded_at = coalesce(key_usage_recorded_at, now()), updated_at = now()
  where workspace_id = p_workspace_id
    and key_id = p_key_id
    and capture_ref_id = p_batch_id
    and status = 'captured';

  return v_inserted;
end;
